role: UFP power-only sink over USB-C receptacle: 5 V VBUS in, independent 5.1k Rd on CC1 and CC2, no PD, no data, no VCONN, no alt mode
_provenance: P1 g0-sense 2026-08-27. Adapted from reference/interfaces/usbc-pd-sink.json (T6 canon, shipped board); all PD-specific rows dropped - explicit delta list in research/interface-usbc-power-sink.md. New numbers verified directly against USB Type-C Cable and Connector Specification R2.0 (Aug 2019) text (usb.org PDF, read 2026-08-27). Sources per number: research/interface-usbc-power-sink.md
notes: NO HIGH-SPEED NETS AND NO DIFFERENTIAL PAIRS exist on this interface or anywhere on this board: D+/D- are UNCONNECTED (no nets, no pads driven), CC1/CC2 are DC nodes (no PD, so no BMC signalling at all), and VBUS/GND are power. high_speed:[] and diff_pairs:[] are correct-by-design, not omissions. Because D+/D- never become nets, check_diffpair auto-discovery has nothing to find - the architect may safely OMIT diff_pairs from the merged constraints.json (an explicit [] there would disable the check board-wide, which is also harmless on this board but is the architect's call, not this fragment's).

Rd RULE (the one non-negotiable): one 5.1 kohm resistor from CC1 to GND AND a second, SEPARATE 5.1 kohm resistor from CC2 to GND. USB Type-C R2.0 4.5.2.2.3.1 (Unattached.SNK Requirements): 'Both CC1 and CC2 pins shall be independently terminated to ground through Rd.' Table 4-25 allows 5.1 kohm +/-20% for a sink that never reads CC (the +/-10% row only matters for detecting the 1.5/3.0 A advertisement, which this board does not do); fit ordinary 1% parts. NO series element between connector CC pin and Rd, and never tie CC1 to CC2.

CONSEQUENCE OF A SHARED/SINGLE Rd (documented field failure, Raspberry Pi 4 rev 1.0): with an e-marked cable the cable's Ra (0.8-1.2 kohm, Type-C Table 4-26) lands on the second CC pin; tied to a shared Rd the source reads Ra-like impedance on both lines, classifies the board as an audio accessory, and NEVER ENABLES VBUS. The board appears dead with exactly the better cables (every Apple/100 W cable is e-marked). Independent Rds make the same cable case harmless: Ra sits in parallel with the unused pin's Rd and the source still sees a clean Rd on the CC wire.

CURRENT ENTITLEMENT for a sink that never monitors CC: default USB power only. Type-C R2.0 4.5.2.3.1.1 (PowerDefault.SNK): 'The port shall draw no more than the default USB power from VBUS'; 4.6.2.1: a Power Sinking Device (no data function) attached to a Default-advertising source 'may draw up to 500 mA'; 1.5 A / 3.0 A may be drawn ONLY by a sink that monitors vRd and adjusts within tSinkAdj. SAFE DESIGN ASSUMPTION: budget <= 500 mA total from VBUS (on-board tens of mA + 100 mA Qwiic reserve fits with margin). The board is ENTITLED to nothing more from any compliant source; it happens to also work on 1.5/3.0 A sources (they supply a superset).

POWER ENTRY RATIONALE: current_a 1.5 at dt_c 10 sizes VBUS copper for the FAULT/INRUSH case (PTC-protected rail can dwell near 1.5 A before trip), giving 0.800 mm min width on 1 oz (pipeline check_current IPC-2152 table). Steady-state design current is <= 0.5 A (0.250 mm at dT 10 C) - the 0.8 mm rule is deliberate cheap margin, fully routable on this board. Net name VBUS is PROVISIONAL: check_current raises exit 2 on a power net absent from the board - reconcile with the final netlist before P5. GND is deliberately NOT listed (full-budget via demands in every GND cluster otherwise). The +3V3 rail belongs to the power-architect fragment, not this one.

VBUS CAPACITANCE AT THE RECEPTACLE (load-bearing for the input cap): max 10 uF between VBUS and GND pins when not attached - Type-C R2.0 Table 4-3 (VBUS Sink Characteristics). Keep TOTAL effective capacitance on the VBUS node <= 10 uF (a nominal 10 uF X5R derates to ~6-8 uF at 5 V DC bias, so one 10 uF + one 100 nF is compliant and sufficient); put any larger bulk on +3V3 AFTER the LDO. cSnkBulkPd = 100 uF does NOT apply (PD-contract number; no PD here).

VBUS PROTECTION NUMBERS (topology per architect, brief delegates it): TVS stand-off >= 5.5 V (VBUS may sit at 5.5 V at light load per Type-C R2.0 4.4.2), clamp comfortably under the LDO's abs-max input (AMS1117-class Vin max 15 V leaves wide choice; SMF5.0A / PESD5V0 class fits). ORDER (adapted from the PD-sink canon): connector -> TVS -> resettable fuse/PTC -> input cap + LDO. TVS at the connector BEFORE the fuse with a short wide GND return; PTC hold >= 0.5 A, trip <= receptacle contact rating.

UNUSED PINS: D+/D- MAY BE LEFT FLOATING - no Type-C or USB 2.0 rule requires terminating an unimplemented data function on a UFP; the board simply never enumerates (which is exactly why the budget is default power). SBU1/SBU2 float (Type-C Table 4-28: >= 950 kohm to appear open - floating trivially complies). VCONN: none - a receptacle-only Rd sink never sources or consumes VCONN and needs no Ra (Ra lives in the cable plug).

CC ROUTING: unconstrained. With no PD there is no BMC signalling - CC1/CC2 are pure DC divider nodes. Any width, any length; place each Rd anywhere convenient between its CC pin and GND (near the connector is tidy, not required). No CC caps needed (the 200-600 pF PD receiver budget does not apply); a small cap is harmless but pointless.

RECEPTACLE (class constraints; exact part is P3's): USB 2.0-only / power-capable Type-C receptacle, JLC-assemblable, e.g. 16-pin USB 2.0 or 6-pin power-only variant. Land ALL VBUS contacts (A4/A9/B4/B9) and ALL GND contacts (A1/A12/B1/B12) ganged in copper at the pads - ratings are collective nameplate values (GCT class: 5 A collectively = 1.25 A/contact); trivial at 0.5 A but land them anyway for resistance and mechanics. Shell/shield pins: tie DIRECTLY to GND at the connector (single-ground bare board; Type-C R2.0 3.2.1 note 6 connects shield and GND at both plug ends anyway, so isolating the shell buys nothing); give shield legs their own vias into the B.Cu GND pour - they double as retention.

MECHANICAL / BOARD EDGE: prefer a TOP-MOUNT receptacle - needs NO board-edge cutout on a 1.6 mm board (mid-mount variants require a routed notch; avoid unless P3 has a stock reason). Mating face flush with or slightly proud of the board edge: Type-C R2.0 Figure 3-80 requires >= 0.05 mm clearance from product surface to plug overmold for full seating - on a bare board this means zero setback from the outline. Keep a ~13 mm wide swath at the board edge (centered on the connector) free of tall parts so the plug overmold seats (derived from Figure 3-79's 12.85 mm recommended connector pitch - ASSUMED as keepout width). THT shield legs / SMD anchor pads must be soldered (connector checklist: force-loaded connector needs retention).

CREEPAGE/CLEARANCE at 5 V: nothing binds beyond fab minimum. check_creepage's 30 V threshold is never crossed (voltages entry emitted anyway so the checker has the number and a future revision engages automatically). IPC-2221 first band (0-15 V): 0.13 mm exposed lands (A6) / 0.05 mm masked traces (B4) - both below JLC's 2-layer 1 oz minimum clearance of 0.127 mm, which therefore dominates everywhere except pad-to-pad (0.13 mm, met by any manufacturable footprint).

PLACEMENT HINT for P2: the receptacle wants a placement.edges pin (board edge, mating face out) and a sides pin (front, mates from the top) in the merged constraints; corridor from connector to LDO input carries the only meaningful current on the board.
